quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian is one of the few languages in Europe that isn't part of the Indo-European language family—it's actually related to Finnish and Estonian! The Hungarian word for 'butterfly' is 'pillangó,' which sounds a bit like the flutter of wings. Many Hungarians believe that if a butterfly lands on you, it brings good luck and joy.

short_read.title: The Secret Social Lives of Hummingbirds
short_read.teaser: Hummingbirds aren't just solitary nectar-sippers—scientists have discovered they actually remember every flower they've visited and for how long. These tiny birds have remarkable memories and even recognize individual humans who feed them!

medium_read.title: How Gardens Help Us Age with Grace and Joy
medium_read.teaser: Gardening offers far more than beautiful blooms—it's a pathway to better memory, reduced stress, and a deeper sense of purpose as we age. This gentle exploration shows how tending plants tends to our hearts and minds in remarkable ways.

long_read.title: The Silk Road: Ancient Highway of Culture and Commerce
long_read.teaser: For over 1,500 years, the Silk Road connected East and West, carrying not just silk and spices but ideas, art, and innovations that shaped civilizations. This beautifully illustrated journey explores the merchants, travelers, and dreamers who traversed these ancient routes.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season at Ediz Hook
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot harbor seal pups at Ediz Hook! These adorable youngsters are learning to swim and fish alongside their mothers in the protected waters. The best viewing times are during low tide in the early morning or late afternoon—bring binoculars and watch from a respectful distance.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute when it's actively flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're absolutely right—1,200 beats per minute! That tiny heart works incredibly hard to power those rapid wings.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 1,200 beats per minute. That's about 20 times faster than a human heart—remarkable for such a tiny bird!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The answer is 1,200 beats per minute! It's hard to imagine such a tiny heart beating so fast, but that's what powers their incredible hovering flight.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To fuel this incredibly fast heartbeat, hummingbirds must eat about half their body weight in nectar each day. They visit hundreds of flowers daily and can remember each one they've been to!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! That's exactly right! Such a lovely word to express gratitude.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Köszönöm'! It's pronounced 'kuh-suh-num' and is one of the most important words to know in Hungarian.
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian has many beautiful expressions of gratitude. A shorter, casual version is 'köszi,' while 'köszönöm szépen' means 'thank you very much.' The language is known for its warmth and politeness.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree is the most common in Olympic National Park?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Western Hemlock is indeed the most abundant tree in Olympic National Park. These beautiful evergreens thrive in the moist Pacific Northwest climate and can live for over 500 years!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is Western Hemlock! While Douglas Fir, Sitka Spruce, and Western Red Cedar all grow beautifully in the park, Western Hemlock is the most common, especially in the temperate rainforests.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Western Hemlocks are shade-tolerant trees with graceful, drooping branch tips. They're a keystone species in the Olympic forests, providing food and shelter for countless birds, mammals, and insects.
